sentiment.summary: Over the past 30 days, coverage of Ethereum was largely constructive: major asset managers advanced Ether-linked products (Fidelity seeking to add staking and payouts to its ether ETF; Goldman Sachs’ planned NEOS deal cited Bitcoin- and Ether-linked income funds), while the Ethereum Foundation funded WEBCAT under its Trillion Dollar Security effort and announced a board addition. Regulatory news was more mixed, with Russia moving to limit retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether, and USDT under purchase caps for non-qualified investors.

tags.label: ether ETF staking filings
tags.why: Cointelegraph and CoinDesk both report Fidelity filing or moving to add staking and quarterly payouts to its ether ETF, with the fund keeping 85% of staking rewards.

tags.label: institutional Ether-linked ETFs
tags.why: Cointelegraph reports Goldman Sachs plans to acquire NEOS and its ETF business, including Bitcoin- and Ether-linked income funds.

tags.label: security tooling grant
tags.why: The Ethereum Foundation announced a Trillion Dollar Security grant to Freedom of the Press Foundation to continue developing WEBCAT, an open-source browser code-verification tool.

tags.label: retail trading restrictions
tags.why: CoinDesk reports Russia is restricting retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether, and USDT, with a 300,000-ruble annual purchase limit per intermediary for non-qualified investors.

tags.label: EF board update
tags.why: The Ethereum Foundation reported that pcaversaccio joined its board, noting prior ecosystem contributor roles including SEAL 911 and the Silviculture Society.

sentiment.coverage_note: Usable items came from Cointelegraph, CoinDesk, and Ethereum Foundation RSS (all ok); grounding and YouTube returned no results, and Reddit auth-failed, so social and web-grounded coverage is missing.
